MARKET.SalesConcessionDescription: Seller concessions were not considered a major factor for these type properties in this market. Conventional, FHA, & VA financing was considered normal practices of the transaction process with minimal concessions requested in transactions.
MARKET.NeighborhoodMarketabilityFactorsDescript: Short sales, Bank sales, & Reo's are found in the market area due to the current economy. This type of sale is not the predominant sale located in this market area.
MARKET.DataSourceDescription: The Market Conditions Addenda was completed with data from Dayton Area Board of REALTORS MLS with an effective date of 10/05/2026.
MARKET.MarketTrendsReconciliationComment: An analysis was performed of the above information and it is of the appraiser's opinion this data demonstrates that within the previous 90 days the market for these type properties have an overall trend of supply of listings and the total number of sales are in balance with the absorption rate of sales in balance, and the months of housing supply decreasing. The housing supply seems to be slightly low with factors attributed to the rise and fall of the median sales price. The median list to sale ratios seemed to have remained relatively stable, with these type of properties showing slight fluctuations in sales prices. The limited number sales for this area makes this data less reliable for valuation purposes.

VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription:
Digital signatures have been used in this appraisal for the purpose of electronic transmission and is in accordance with reporting requirements of the uniform standards of professional appraisal practice. This digitized image of the appraisers signature is controlled by a personalized identification number where the appraiser has sole personalized control of affixing the signature. Electronically affixing a signature to the certification in a report carries the same level of authenticity and responsibility as an ink signature on paper.
The intended user of this appraisal report is the lender/client. The intended use is to evaluate the property that is the subject of this appraisal for a mortgage finance transaction, subject to the stated scope of work, purpose of the appraisal, reporting requirements of this appraisal report form and the definition of market value. This report contains sufficient information to enable the lender/client to understand the report. Any other party receiving a copy of this report for any reason is not an intended user; nor does receiving a copy of this report result in an appraiser-client relationship. Use of this report by any other party(ies) is not intended by the appraiser. No additional intended users are identified by the appraiser.
This appraisal is not a home inspection and the appraiser is not acting as a home inspector when preparing the report.
"Extraordinary Assumption and Limiting Condition:" The repairs are based only on a visual inspection of any-all items noted. Any reported findings are based on readily observable findings at the time of property visit. The appraiser is not a home inspector, building contractor or engineer. The appraiser is not qualified or competent to detect items not readily observable. Any users of this report having concerns about structural integrity, mechanical, infestation, contamination or other issues about the subject property are urged to consult the services of an expert, or person trained in the particular field (s) of concern. It could, if found to be false, alter the appraiser's opinions or conclusions.
Gross Area Calculations: The GLA is based on measurements made by the appraiser at the time of inspection. The measurement technique used is based on the American National Standard for single family residential buildings (ANSI Z765-2021). However, due to variations associated with on-site measurements (tape stretching, obstructions, second level insets, knee walls, and non-square areas), GLA calculations are approximate. According to the American National Standards Institute the above grade finished square footage of a dwelling is the sum of the finished areas of levels that are entirely above grade. The below grade finished square footage of a house is the sum of finished areas on levels that are wholly or partly below grade. Subject is measured to one tenth of a foot per ANSI standard.
"Highest and Best Use" is a Land Use Analysis that concludes maximum productivity of a site "as improved". Tests applies to the site as vacant and as improved are conclusions of Physical Possible Uses that are Legally Permissible and Economically Feasible resulting in the maximum productivity conclusion. In the Site Section, the physical and legal characteristics are summarized as are the improvements in the Improvement Section of the URAR. The economic conclusion of marketability is made in comparison with the conclusions of central tendencies and Market Conditions reported in the Neighborhood Section of the URAR. From these separate analyses, Market, Site and Improvement, the appraiser concluded that as improved, in its currently use, the subject is in its Highest and Best Use, as reported.

COST_ANALYSIS._Comment: Physical Depreciation is calculated using the effective age/economic life method. No significant functional obsolescence or external depreciation was noted. Land/improvement ratio is typical for the area. Total economic life is market abstracted at 60 years and has implications for both the cost and sales comparison approaches. Replacement Cost data is developed from market abstraction with Marshall & Swift. Site value was derived using the extraction method.
